answer: On an island, all work is filed in one crystal lattice: each job is a node linked to the three jobs it builds on. To earn full rights, a newcomer adds twenty nodes, each checked by three random peers who re-run part of the cited work. A forged link shows at once: the cited job does not exist or does not fit. Each newcomer locks a 40-token walnut deposit, forfeited on the first forged citation, half to the peer who caught it. Faking a hundred identities means two thousand genuine jobs and four thousand tokens at risk, more than the fakes could collect.
